name: Famille Isabel Ferrando Châteauneuf-du-Pape Colombis 2015
text:
## Famille Isabel Ferrando Châteauneuf-du-Pape Colombis 2015

**The story.** Isabel Ferrando never planned to make wine. Her first career was in banking, but she changed course, learned winemaking in [Gigondas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigondas_AOC) at Domaine Raspail-Ay, and in 2004 bought 3.9 hectares of vines in the southern part of [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC). She brought in the consultant Philippe Cambie, and from that first 2004 vintage the wines have been, in Jeff Leve's words, "on fire". She also owns Domaine Saint Préfert, and wanted Colombis to show a different terroir from it ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). The estate has been certified [organic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_farming) since 2012 ([Premium Vins](https://www.premiumvins.com.au/shop/category/domaine-isabel-ferrando)).

**The wine: Colombis.** Colombis is 100% old-vine [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), from vines 60 to over 100 years old on mostly sandy soils with some clay, in three lieux-dits that each give about a third of the wine: Colombis (which names the wine), Cristia and Les Roues ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/); [Premium Vins](https://www.premiumvins.com.au/shop/category/domaine-isabel-ferrando)). Yields are about 20 hectolitres per hectare. Since 2009 the grapes have gone into the vat as whole bunches, stems and all, which adds structure. Fermentation lasts about five weeks at 28°C in a conical oak vat, and the wine ages about 18 months in 600-litre demi-muids that are three years old. It is bottled unfiltered. Only about 550 cases are made ([Premium Vins](https://www.premiumvins.com.au/shop/category/domaine-isabel-ferrando); [The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) says Grenache suffered from [coulure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulure) at flowering in 2015 (many flowers failed to set into grapes), so yields were lower but quality very promising, with alcohol higher than in the two previous years. [John Livingstone-Learmonth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Livingstone-Learmonth), writing for [Decanter](https://www.decanter.com/learn/vintage-guides/rhone-vintage-guides/chateauneuf-du-pape-2015-gigondas-vacqueyras-366743/), noted that early September rain was heavy in Châteauneuf, which favoured free-draining sandy soils. That suits Colombis, which grows mostly on sand.

**What the critics say for 2015.** As listed by the Australian importer [Premium Vins](https://www.premiumvins.com.au/shop/category/domaine-isabel-ferrando) (checked on its page):
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 96.** From some of the appellation's cooler sites and 60- to 80-year-old vines, "a stunner": a true sense of [garrigue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garrigue), dark fruit, peppery spice and rich, velvety tannins. Drink 2017 to 2030.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 95.** A gorgeous texture, with very fine tannins wrapped around blackberry, raspberry and plum, and licorice, black tea and graphite on a long finish. Tempting young, but better with cellaring. Best 2020 to 2040.
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 95.** More open and sexy, from very old vines on sand: raspberry ("framboise"), incense, potpourri and flowers; pretty, elegant and complex, with sweet fruit and polished tannins. Happy drinking over 10 to 15 years.
- **La Revue du Vin de France: 18/20.**
- **Jeff Leve, [The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/): 97** (from the vintage list on his producer page).
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.8** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. The Wine Advocate suggested drinking by 2030, Dunnuck over 10 to 15 years, and Wine Spectator up to 2040; The Wine Cellar Insider says Colombis drinks best from 4 to 18 years after the vintage. So it is in its prime now. An elegant, whole-bunch Grenache from sand should be perfumed and silky at this age. Decant about an hour ahead, and plan to drink it over the next few years.

**Serving.** The Wine Cellar Insider suggests about 15.5°C, almost cellar temperature, for freshness and lift, and 1 to 2 hours in a [decanter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation) when young; older bottles need only enough to leave the sediment behind ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). Use a large Burgundy-style glass to show off the perfume.

**Food.** The Wine Cellar Insider suggests classic meat dishes (veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, game, roast chicken, braises, sausages, barbecue and [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet)), plus tuna, mushrooms, eggplant, tomatoes and cheese. For this perfumed Grenache, my picks are a roast leg of lamb with [herbes de Provence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbes_de_Provence), duck breast with cherries, [ratatouille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratatouille), or a mushroom [risotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risotto). I'd avoid very spicy food.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists Colombis. With about 550 cases a year, it is, as Leve says, hard to find once it has been on the market a few years, so look for it at auction and with fine-wine merchants.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V), a former Archbishop of Bordeaux, moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k), beginning the [Avignon Papacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy). His successor [John XXII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXII) improved the vineyards to the north and built the summer [castle](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Ch%C3%A2teau+des+Papes,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k) that gave the village its name, "the Pope's new castle". The wine became known as "Vin du Pape" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Phylloxera.** The [phylloxera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_French_Wine_Blight) louse reached Châteauneuf in the early 1870s, earlier than most French regions, and wiped out the vineyards. Before the First World War, much of the replanted wine was sold to [Burgundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundy_wine) as "vin de médecine" to strengthen thinner wines ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **France's first appellation.** Fraud was so common in the early 20th century that local growers, led by Baron [Pierre Le Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Roy_de_Boiseaumari%C3%A9) of [Château Fortia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Fortia), drew up France's first [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) rules in 1923, made law on 15 May 1936. One of the baron's rules: vines could only be planted on land dry enough to grow both [lavender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavandula) and [thyme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thyme) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **From banking to Grenache.** Isabel Ferrando's switch from finance to wine in the early 2000s, and her first vintage in 2004, made Colombis one of the newer stars of an appellation whose family estates often go back centuries ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

**Curious details**
- **800 bottles of Cinsault.** Ferrando's rarest wine, F601, first made in 2018, is 100% old-vine [Cinsault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinsaut) planted in 1928 on very fine sand with [quartz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz) over blue clay. It is named after its parcel, and only about 800 bottles are made ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/domaine-ferrando-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).
- **All stems in.** In the very ripe 2009 and 2010 vintages, Colombis was made entirely from whole bunches, and the grapes haven't been destemmed since.
- **Cambie again.** Colombis is one of several top wines in this cellar shaped by the consultant Philippe Cambie, along with Le Clos du Caillou and Les Halos de Jupiter.
- **The famous stones.** Much of Châteauneuf is covered in [galets roulés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galets_roul%C3%A9s), smooth [quartzite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartz) stones left by Alpine glaciers and rounded over millennia by the [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne). They soak up the sun by day and give the heat back to the vines at night, and in dry summers they help keep moisture in the soil ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **The flying-cigar law.** In 1954, after local reports of [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_saucer), the Châteauneuf council banned "flying cigars" from flying over or landing in the commune. The decree is still in force, and a Californian Rhône-style wine from [Bonny Doon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonny_Doon_Vineyard), Le Cigare Volant, is named after the tale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Strong by law.** Châteauneuf must reach at least 12.5% alcohol with no added sugar, and most wines come in at 14 to 15.5%. Yields are limited to 35 hectolitres per hectare, nearly half what [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine) allows ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
